paragraphs.source_en: When I came to my senses, I was floating on the surface of the water. Not knowing what to do, I clawed wildly, but all I could claw at was water, and the moment I did, I sank. There was nothing for it, so I kicked up with my hind legs and paddled with my forelegs; this had some effect at last, the water splashed noisily, and my head finally rose above the surface. I looked around me. Where on earth was I? Ah, I had fallen into the water jar. Until summer this jar had been filled with a water plant called mizu-aoi, but after summer the crows came, ate up every bit of it, and even bathed in the jar. Each time Kan the crow took a bath, the water went down; once it had gone down enough, the crows stopped coming. I had just been thinking that lately, with the water so much lower, one hardly saw the crows; who could have imagined that I myself would take their place and bathe here?

paragraphs.source_en: From the water’s surface to the rim of the jar was well over ten centimeters, and even stretching out my legs I could not reach it. I sprang upward, but it was no use. If I simply kept still, my body only sank lower and lower. However I struggled, all I managed was to make my claws scrape noisily against the wall of the jar. Sometimes, when I struck the side, I seemed to float up a little, but the moment I slipped I went plunging down again with a splash. Once I went under, the suffocation was unbearable, so I clawed at the jar again. By then my body was growing ever more exhausted; my mind was frantic, and my legs no longer obeyed me so well. In the end, was I clawing at the jar in order to go under? Or was I going under in order to claw at the jar? Even I could no longer tell.

paragraphs.source_en: At that moment, in the midst of extreme agony, I thought: “The reason I am suffering this torment is simply that I want to climb out of the jar. I long desperately to get out, yet I know perfectly well that I cannot. My forelegs are less than ten centimeters long; even if my body floats on the water and I stretch those forelegs from that floating point with all my might, my claws cannot reach the rim, fully fifteen centimeters above. Since my claws cannot catch the rim, no matter how I splash and fret, even if I struggled for a hundred years, there is absolutely no way I can escape from this jar. To try to get out when I know I cannot is plainly to insist on doing the impossible. Because I insist on doing this impossible thing, I am suffering so much. How pointless! To seek out suffering for myself, to willingly submit myself to this torment, is that not the height of stupidity?”

paragraphs.source_en: Gradually I began to feel more at ease. I could no longer tell whether it was pain or gratitude to heaven, nor whether I was in the water or in my master’s sitting room. Wherever I was, whatever was happening, it no longer mattered. I felt only ease. No, I could no longer even feel ease. Even if heaven and earth were ground to dust, I had in any case entered a strange and tranquil world. I am about to die. By dying, I have obtained this serenity; without dying, such serenity cannot be obtained. Namu Amida Butsu, Namu Amida Butsu. How grateful, how grateful.
